AddTokenParams.description:
`AddToken` (API 1.1): adds one ERC-20 token or SPL mint to the
configuration, with its decimals (and, on EVM chains, its symbol) read
from the chain.

| | |
|---|---|
| Access | payments client allowlist |
| Auth | agent token, verified by the signer daemon |
| Response | [`PaymentsRpcResponse::TokenAdded`](crate::payments::PaymentsRpcResponse::TokenAdded) |
| Side effects | reads the chain; atomically rewrites the service's `config.json` unless the token is already configured |
| Idempotent | yes: adding the same contract or mint on the same network again changes nothing |
| Since | API 1.1.0 (capability `AddToken`) |

Lets a client add a token by network and address without doing chain I/O
or a `GetConfig` / edit / `SetConfig` round trip itself.

# Steps

1. `network` must name a configured chain. `address` must be a contract
   (EVM: `0x` + 40 hex characters, mixed case only with a valid checksum;
   stored lower case) or a mint (Solana: a base58 public key). Native coins
   are refused: the zero address, `0xeeee...eeee`, and the system program.
   `symbol` is 1 to 32 characters without control characters, and
   `decimals` is at most 36.
2. If a token already has a deployment on `network` at `address`, the call
   returns that token unchanged (`added: false`) without reading the chain;
   `symbol` and `decimals` are ignored.
3. The service reads the chain through the network's `rpc_url`. EVM: the
   endpoint's chain id must match, the address must hold contract code,
   and `decimals()` and `symbol()` are called. Solana: the endpoint must
   serve the configured cluster, and the mint account must exist, belong to
   the SPL Token or Token-2022 program, and have no transfer hook; its
   decimals are read. SPL mints have no on-chain symbol, so `symbol` is
   required on Solana chains (checked before any chain I/O).
4. Decimals: the chain's value. A `decimals` that differs from it is
   refused. If the chain cannot be read (no `rpc_url`, endpoint
   unreachable or for another chain, `decimals()` failing), the given
   `decimals` is used unverified (`verified_on_chain: false`); without one
   the call fails with `ChainRpc`.
5. Symbol: `symbol` when given, else the on-chain `symbol()` (EVM). The
   token's display `name` is the symbol.
6. Key: the symbol in lower case, with every run of characters outside
   `[a-z0-9._-]` replaced by `-` (dropped at either end; `token` if
   nothing is left). If that token exists without a deployment on
   `network`, the deployment is added to it; if it exists with another deployment on `network`, the key gets
   the suffix `-` + the first 6 characters of the address after `0x` (or
   of the mint), in lower case; otherwise a new token is created with no
   `recommended_limits`.
7. The resulting configuration is validated as a whole, exactly like
   `SetConfig`, and stored atomically.

Adding a token never changes what the signer daemon's policies allow.

**Errors:** `AgentAuthenticationFailed`, `SignerUnavailable`, `Signer`;
`InvalidRequest` (unknown network, malformed or native address, invalid
symbol or decimals, no symbol for a Solana mint or for an EVM token
without an on-chain `symbol()`, no contract at the address, a missing or
unsupported mint, `decimals` that differ from the chain's, both candidate
keys taken); `ChainRpc` (the chain could not be read and no `decimals` was
given; the message says how to set a working `rpc_url` or pass
`decimals`); `InvalidConfig` (the result fails validation, for example a
257th token); `Persistence`.

  "method": "AddToken",
  "params": {
    "auth": {

LookupTokenParams.description:
`LookupToken` (API 1.1): reads an ERC-20 token's or SPL mint's metadata
from the chain without changing anything and without agent credentials.

| | |
|---|---|
| Access | payments client allowlist (the peer uid is checked by the socket) |
| Auth | none |
| Response | [`PaymentsRpcResponse::TokenInfo`](crate::payments::PaymentsRpcResponse::TokenInfo) |
| Side effects | none: reads the chain, never changes the configuration |
| Idempotent | yes |
| Since | API 1.1.0 (capability `LookupToken`) |

The read and validation half of [`AddToken`](AddTokenParams), with the
same rules for `network`, `address` (native coins refused), `symbol`,
`decimals`, the contract-code check, and an unreadable chain (steps 1,
3, 4, and 5 there). It never answers from the configuration: the token
is read from the chain even when it is configured. A client can verify a
token before agent credentials exist, for example while setting up
spending limits.

**Why no credentials are needed:** it reads only public chain data,
only through the RPC endpoints the configuration already names (its
`rpc_url` and `fallback_rpc_urls`, never a URL from the request), stores
nothing, signs nothing, and asks the signer daemon nothing. The socket
still admits only allowlisted peers.

**Errors:** `InvalidRequest`, `ChainRpc` (as for `AddToken`).

Request:

```json
{
  "method": "LookupToken",
  "params": {
    "network": "bsc",
    "address": "0x8AC76a51cc950d9822D68b83fE1Ad97B32Cd580d"
  }
}

```

Response:

```json
{
  "type": "TokenInfo",
  "data": {
    "network": "bsc",
    "chain_id": 56,
    "address": "0x8ac76a51cc950d9822d68b83fe1ad97b32cd580d",
    "symbol": "USDC",
    "decimals": 18,
    "verified_on_chain": true
  }
}

```

| Auth | agent token, verified by the signer daemon |
| Response | [`MppResponse`] |

ReleaseSignedNonceParams.description:
`ReleaseSignedNonce`: returns the nonce of a signed `BroadcastTx` that
never reached the network, so the next transaction does not leave a gap.

| | |
|---|---|
| Access | agent allowlist |
| Auth | agent token; the transaction must have been signed for this agent |
| Response | [`DaemonRpcResponse::Unit`](crate::DaemonRpcResponse::Unit) |
| Side effects | forgets the signed transaction, returns its nonce to the pool (unless it is reserved again), drops the recorded signature so a retry of the signing request cannot return it, consumes `request_id` |
| Idempotent | yes per `request_id`: resending the identical request succeeds again |

Signing a `BroadcastTx` consumes its nonce: the daemon never hands it out
again, so if the send fails, the next transaction gets the following nonce
and waits forever behind the gap. This method closes the gap.

**Only call it when the transaction certainly never reached a node**: the
`eth_sendRawTransaction` request could not be delivered (the connection
was refused), the node answered it with a JSON-RPC error (nodes do not
relay transactions they reject), or it was never sent at all (for example
the signed transaction failed local verification). After a timeout, a lost
response, or an HTTP error from a proxy, the node may have the transaction,
so keep the nonce. A released nonce is handed out again, and a second
transaction with the same nonce replaces or races the first: both were
allowed by policy, and at most one can be mined.

The spend stays counted against the agent's daily and weekly limits: the
daemon cannot see the network, and refunding it on the agent's word would
let an agent that broadcasts the transaction itself spend past its limits.
A transaction can be released once, within 10 minutes of signing.

**Errors:** `AgentAuthenticationFailed` (also when another agent signed the
transaction), `InvalidRequestTimestamps`, `RequestExpired`,
`RequestReplayDetected`, `TooManyTrackedReplayIds`,
`UnknownSignedTransaction` (not signed by this daemon, already released,
or signed more than 10 minutes ago), `InvalidNonceReservation` (`chain_id`
or `nonce` do not match the transaction, or a malformed hash),
`Persistence`.

```json

  "method": "ReleaseSignedNonce",
  "params": {
    "request": {
      "request_id": "4d3c2b1a-0f9e-4d8c-8b7a-695847362514",
      "agent_key_id": "9a8b7c6d-5e4f-4a3b-8c2d-1e0f9a8b7c6d",
      "agent_auth_token": "8c1e5f0b2a7d4e3c9b6a1f8e2d7c4b0a.f3e2d1c0b9a8476594a3b2c1d0e9f8a7",

      "requested_at": [2026, 309, 12, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0],
      "expires_at": [2026, 309, 12, 2, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0]
    }
  }
}

```

```json
{
  "type": "Unit"
}

```

ResumeApprovedParams.description:
`ResumeApproved`: continue a call that returned `ManualApprovalPending`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Access | payments client allowlist |
| Auth | agent token of the agent that made the original call |
| Response | what the original call returns: [`EvmSignature`], [`EvmTransaction`], or again [`ManualApprovalPending`] |
| Side effects | as for the original call; removes the pending-approval record once the request is decided |
| Idempotent | no: a completed resume removes the record |

first checks that the stored nonce is still unused on chain and reserves
exactly that nonce again; then it verifies, sends, and waits as the
original call asked. While the request is still pending the result is
`ManualApprovalPending` again. A rejected request fails with `Signer` /
`ManualApprovalRejected`. The record is removed once the resume succeeds
or fails for good, and kept after `SignerUnavailable`, `ChainRpc`, and `Persistence` errors so
the call can be retried. Records of other agents are invisible
(`UnknownPendingApproval`).

`UnknownPendingApproval`, `InvalidRequest` (the nonce was used meanwhile),

SignRequest.description:
Request sent by an agent to evaluate, explain, or sign an [`AgentAction`].

Freshness rules (checked by the daemon): `requested_at < expires_at`,
`expires_at` in the future, `requested_at` at most 30 s ahead of the
daemon clock, and `expires_at - requested_at` at most 5 minutes.

action.description: Semantic action details used by policy checks.

payload.description:
Payload bytes as a JSON array of byte values (0-255), at most 32 KiB.

Security contract: payload must be the canonical compact JSON encoding
of `action` (`serde_json::to_vec(&action)`: struct fields in declaration
order, no whitespace); the daemon rejects semantic or byte-level
mismatches with `PayloadActionMismatch`.

request_id.description:
Client-generated unique request identifier (UUID v4 recommended).

A signed request id is consumed: reusing it with a different payload
fails with `RequestReplayDetected`, while resending the identical
request returns the recorded signature (idempotent retry).

SignTypedDataParams.description:
`SignTypedData`: sign EIP-712 typed data under the agent's policies.

| | |
|---|---|
| Access | payments client allowlist |
| Auth | agent token, verified by the signer daemon |
| Response | [`EvmSignature`] or [`ManualApprovalPending`] |
| Side effects | a signature; a pending-approval record |
| Idempotent | no |

`typed_data_json` is the `eth_signTypedData_v4` JSON object as a string;
its `domain.chainId` is required. Typed data that no `Eip712Signing`
policy covers needs manual approval. The result's `signature_hex` is the
65-byte `r || s || v` signature with `v` = 27 or 28.

**Errors:** `AgentAuthenticationFailed`, `SignerUnavailable`, `Signer`,
`InvalidRequest`, `Persistence`.

`fee_payer` may be someone other than the agent (a merchant's fee payer).
The daemon then signs only the agent's slot and returns a partially signed
transaction whose fee-payer signature is all zero; the fee payer adds its
signature before broadcasting.

`SetComputeUnitPrice` (when set), `SetComputeUnitLimit` (when set), the
primary transfer, the `memo` (when set), then for each split in order: its
`CreateIdempotent` (when `create_ata`), its transfer, its memo (when set).
SOL transfers are System `Transfer`s; SPL transfers are `TransferChecked`
from the agent's associated token account.

Policies see one payment: the sum of all legs, in `asset`, to the primary
recipient, on the Solana policy network. Recipient scopes must cover every
leg's recipient.

WireDaemonError.description:
Serializable daemon error, one kind per failure the daemon can report.

The `kind` names are stable within a major API version.

oneOf.description:
An admin proof was rejected: a challenge signature did not verify, or
a lease secret (or the lease's peer euid) did not match.
`{"kind": "AuthenticationFailed"}`.

An admin method was called by a non-root peer without a lease.
`{"kind": "AdminAuthenticationRequired"}`.

The method is reserved for root peers (`EnrollAdminCredential`).
`{"kind": "RootPeerRequired"}`.

The presented lease id is unknown (never issued, revoked, or forgotten
on daemon restart), or `RevokeAdminLease` named an unknown lease.
The presented lease has expired; obtain a new one.
The daemon already holds the maximum number of active leases (64).
No admin credential has this id. `{"kind": "UnknownAdminCredential", "data": "<uuid>"}`.

The credential payload was invalid (bad SEC1 key, bad label, already
enrolled). `data` is a human-readable reason.
Enrollment refused: the credential limit was reached.

The challenge is unknown, expired, already used, or was begun by a
different peer euid.

The challenge `purpose` is not 1-128 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9._:/-]`.
`data` is a human-readable reason.
Too many unanswered challenges are pending.
The credential is locked for 30 seconds after 5 failed signatures.
No vault key has this id. `data` is the id.
No agent key has this id. `data` is the id.
No policy has this id. `data` is the id.
No (retained) manual approval request has this id. `data` is the id.

The agent key id is unknown, the token does not match, or the agent
does not own the referenced reservation.
`payload` is not the canonical JSON encoding of `action`.
`payload` exceeds the daemon limit.

max_bytes.description: Maximum payload size in bytes (32 KiB by default).

oneOf.description:
`requested_at`/`expires_at` violate the freshness rules (ordering,
30-second clock skew, 5-minute maximum lifetime).
`expires_at` is in the past.
The `request_id` was already used for a different request.
The replay-protection table is full; retry later.

The policy attachment is invalid (empty set, disabled policy, or an
agent/vault key mismatch). `data` is a human-readable reason.
The nonce reservation request is invalid. `data` is a human-readable reason.
Too many active nonce reservations.
The reservation would skip too far past the tracked nonce head.

requested_skip.description: Number of nonces the request would have skipped.

oneOf.description: No active reservation has this id. `data` is the id.
A `BroadcastTx` was submitted without an active reservation of its nonce.

chain_id.description: EVM chain id of the transaction.

oneOf.description:
The policy payload is invalid (validation failure or duplicate id).
`data` is a human-readable reason.

The action failed domain validation (bad address, unrecognized
calldata, inconsistent Tempo channel, ...). `data` is a human-readable reason.

The request is held for an operator decision. Not a failure: approve
the request (`DecideManualApprovalRequest`), then resend the same
action (a fresh `request_id` and timestamps are fine).
An operator rejected the approval request for this action.
The approval request was already decided or completed.
The agent already has the maximum number of pending approval requests.

agent_key_id.description: Agent key that owns the pending requests.

max_pending.description: Maximum pending requests per agent key (64 by default).

`reuse`.
The daemon holds no wallet (vault key) to reuse or back up.

The wallet operation is ambiguous or inconsistent (for example several
vault keys and no `vault_key_id`). `data` is a human-readable reason.
A spending limit row is invalid. `data` is a human-readable reason.

The backup document is not a valid wallet backup (malformed, an
unsupported version or KDF parameters, or metadata that does not match
the decrypted key). `data` is a human-readable reason.

The backup could not be decrypted: the passphrase is wrong or the
document was altered (the two are indistinguishable).
A new backup's passphrase is too short.

`ReleaseSignedNonce` named a transaction this daemon did not sign for
the agent, already released, or signed more than 10 minutes ago.
`data` is the transaction hash.
The policy engine denied the request. `data` is a [`PolicyError`].
The signer backend failed. `data` is a [`SignerError`].
The daemon configuration is invalid. `data` is a human-readable reason.
Internal locking failure; the daemon should be restarted.

A transport or serialization failure inside the daemon. `data` is a
human-readable reason.

Persisting daemon state failed; the change was rolled back. `data` is a

WirePaymentsError.description:
Serializable payments service error (`WireResponse.ok == false`).

JSON: `{"kind": "<Kind>"}` for kinds without data, otherwise
`{"kind": "<Kind>", "data": ...}`. The `kind` names are stable within a
major API version; new kinds may be added in minor versions, so clients
must treat an unknown `kind` as a generic failure.

oneOf.description:
The signer daemon rejected the agent credentials (unknown agent key or
wrong token). `{"kind": "AgentAuthenticationFailed"}`.

The signer daemon could not be reached or answered with something the
service did not understand. Retry later; check that the signer daemon
is running. `data` is a human-readable reason.

The signer daemon refused a request made on the agent's behalf, for
example a policy denial or a rejected manual approval. `data` is the
signer daemon's own error, unchanged.

A signature is still waiting for an operator's decision after the
service stopped waiting. Approve or reject the request, then resend the
same call.

oneOf.description:
The configuration failed validation; nothing was changed. `data` is a
human-readable reason.

Saving the service's state failed; nothing was changed. `data` is a
human-readable reason.

The request is well-formed but cannot be carried out as asked, for
example an unknown or wrong-family network, an amount with too many
decimals, or a missing token account. Nothing was signed. `data` is a
human-readable reason.

A chain RPC call failed or returned something unusable (unreachable
endpoint, wrong cluster, rejected transaction). Retrying may help.
`data` is a human-readable reason that never includes the RPC URL.

The transaction the signer daemon returned does not match the
request, so the service refused to return or broadcast it. This
indicates a bug or tampering; do not retry blindly. `data` names the
mismatching field.

`ResumeApproved` names no pending approval stored for this agent:
never created, already completed, or created by another agent.

The paid HTTP endpoint (the merchant) failed: it could not be
reached or timed out, or it answered with a payment challenge,
receipt, or management response the service cannot accept
(malformed, unsupported, or inconsistent with what was paid). `data`
is a human-readable reason that says whether anything was signed.
An unexpected internal failure. `data` is a human-readable reason.

WireRequest.description:
Client-to-daemon envelope: the only JSON object a client ever sends.

JSON: `{"body_json": "{\"method\":\"Hello\"}"}`.

body_json.description:
A [`DaemonRpcRequest`](crate::DaemonRpcRequest) serialized as a JSON
string. May contain secrets (agent tokens, lease secrets): clients
should wipe it after sending.

WireResponse.description:
Daemon-to-client envelope: the only JSON object the daemon ever sends.

JSON (success): `{"ok": true, "body_json": "{\"type\":\"Unit\"}"}`.
JSON (failure): `{"ok": false, "body_json": "{\"kind\":\"UnknownLease\"}"}`.

ok.description:
`true` when `body_json` holds a `DaemonRpcResponse`, `false` when it
holds a `WireDaemonError`.

X402FetchParams.description:
`X402Fetch`: fetch a URL, paying an x402 `402` answer.

| Access | payments client allowlist |
| Auth | agent token, verified by the signer daemon |
| Response | [`X402Response`] |
| Side effects | HTTP requests to `url`; on a `402`, one policy-checked EIP-3009 signature (spend recorded by the signer daemon) that the merchant can settle on chain |
| Idempotent | no: every paid call is a new payment |

See the [module documentation](self) for the flow.

**Errors:** `AgentAuthenticationFailed`, `SignerUnavailable`, `Signer`
(policy denial, rejected approval, ...), `ManualApprovalPending`,

How long to wait for an operator when a policy requires manual
approval, in seconds (default 0, capped at 600).

expected_amount.description:
Only pay a requirement of exactly this amount, in the asset's base
units (the requirement's own unit).

max_amount.description: Never pay a requirement above this amount, in the asset's base units.

method.description: HTTP method; default `GET`, or `POST` with a body.

payment.description: The payment made; `null` when the first response was not a `402`.

response.description:
The final response: the paid retry's, or the first one when it was
not a `402`.

amount.description: Amount authorized, in the asset's base units.

chain_id.description: EVM chain id of that network.

network.description:
The requirement's network as the merchant named it: a v1 name
(`"base-sepolia"`) or a v2 CAIP-2 id (`"eip155:84532"`).

payment_response.description:
The merchant's decoded `PAYMENT-RESPONSE` (v2) or `X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE`
(v1) header: its settlement result, typically
`{"success": true, "transaction": "0x...", "network": ..., "payer": ...}`.
`null` when the header is missing; a header that is not base64 JSON is
returned as a string.

x402_version.description: x402 protocol version of the merchant's `402` (1 or 2).

description: Wire types of the AgentPay daemon API.
